subject: Draft Annex: snapshot custody, operator access & evidence handover — NexaHealth
messages:
From: Emma Collins <emma.collins@nexahealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nexahealth.com
Date: 2027-09-06T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Draft Annex: snapshot custody, operator access & evidence handover — NexaHealth

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for sending the draft annex earlier today. Our legal and infra teams reviewed and came back with a short list of asks we need clarified before we proceed to signature:

- Operator access: we need a tighter definition of "operator" and explicit limits on remote console sessions and timeboxed maintenance windows.
- Snapshot custody: Nexa requires the ability to verify a point-in-time snapshot of model artifacts and keying state for a 3rd-party audit. We are proposing a quarterly snapshot delivery with an attestation and a read-only witness session.
- Evidence handover: we'd like a clear process for handing over runbooks, logs, and a minimal evidence bundle in the event of contract termination or incident.

I've attached our annotated draft (Nexa_Annex_Draft_v3.pdf) and an evidence checklist from procurement. Can you confirm what Redwood is willing to provide vs. redline? Also who on your side will own the technical evidence questions?

Best,
Emma Collins
Senior Procurement Manager, NexaHealth
emma.collins@nexahealth.com

Attachments: Nexa_Annex_Draft_v3.pdf (PDF, 142KB); evidence-checklist.pdf (PDF, 68KB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Collins <emma.collins@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-06T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft Annex: snapshot custody, operator access & evidence handover — NexaHealth

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (legal) and Karthik (security/ops) to give concrete redlines and an evidence delivery proposal. High-level response now:

- Operator definition: agree we should precisely define "operator" and limit remote interactive sessions to named operator roles for escalations and maintenance only.
- Snapshots: we can provide periodic immutable snapshots (metadata + checksums) and support an audited witness session, but we need to preserve production isolation and cannot hand over private keys or HSM-resident secrets.
- Evidence handover: we can commit to an evidence bundle (runbooks, access logs, snapshot checksums, test harness) on termination with a formal request window and an acceptance test.

Laura/Karthik — can you take the attached Nexa draft and mark the clauses we can accept as-is, propose alternate language where needed, and list any evidence items that we cannot provide for security/legal reasons? Emma — if you can confirm target SLA for delivery and the prospective auditors (internal or named 3rd party), that will help.

I can set up a 30-min sync early next week if useful.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Emma Collins <emma.collins@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-07T11:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft Annex: snapshot custody, operator access & evidence handover — NexaHealth

Thanks Priyom/Emma — I reviewed the Nexa_Annex_Draft_v3.pdf and the procurement checklist. High-level notes and proposed redlines:

1) Operator access (proposed new language): define "Operator" as Redwood personnel with a named role (e.g., "On-call Operator") and require prior written consent for any live interactive session beyond emergency maintenance. All interactive sessions will be recorded and retained per the Order Form retention schedule.

2) Snapshot custody and auditor access: we can accept a quarterly immutable snapshot of model artifacts (metadata + checksums + execution logs) for audit purposes under a non-disclosure and limited-use covenant. We cannot provide HSM private keys or unencrypted training data. For auditor access, we will host a read-only witness session (30–90 minutes) where Redwood demonstrates snapshot integrity; auditor may run predefined verification scripts but not arbitrary commands.

3) Evidence handover on termination: Redwood will deliver an "Evidence Bundle" containing runbooks, configuration manifests, VM/container manifests, snapshot checksums, and redacted operator logs. We will require a 30-day request notice and will perform a mutual acceptance test with the customer's appointed engineer.

4) Insurance & liability carveouts: propose explicit limits tied to the Order Form and exclude forensic obligations that require disclosure of privileged internal processes.

5) Escrow alternative: rather than third-party code escrow, we propose a quarterly signed snapshot transfer plus capability to initiate a documented on-site witness (commercial terms to be priced).

Karthik — below I list the items I need you to confirm which are safe to include in the Evidence Bundle and which must be redacted or summarized for security compliance:
- Operator session recordings (retain/partial redaction)
- Encryption key metadata (key IDs, rotation schedule) — provide metadata only, not key material
- Full access logs (provide filtered, time-bounded slices)

Emma — attached is a marked-up PDF with clause-by-clause comments and a proposed alternate paragraph for the snapshot/audit section. If Nexa can accept the 30-day request window and the "read-only witness" constraint, we can move to a signature-ready annex and separately price the optional on-site witness.

I'll be available for a short call Wednesday morning.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachments: Nexa_Annex_Draft_v3_marked.pdf (PDF, 185KB)

From: Emma Collins <emma.collins@nexahealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-09T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft Annex: snapshot custody, operator access & evidence handover — NexaHealth

Laura/Priyom — thanks, that level of detail helps. Procurement is OK with the read-only witness and 30-day request window, provided we get an explicit list of items that will be redacted and an estimated turnaround time for the Evidence Bundle (we'd like 10 business days after request acceptance). Also: the auditor for this engagement is a named third party (Verity Audit Services). They will want the ability to execute the predefined verification scripts during the witness session.

Next steps: can Redwood send final proposed clause language for the annex and a brief SOW that captures the on-site witness option and pricing? I'll send a short DocuSign envelope to loop in our GC once we have your final wording.

Thanks — Emma
